title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-morgan
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent issue where SSE responses stall mid-stream under p95 load for multi-part responses (long streaming generation).
- Observed partial chunks not flushed for 2-8s, then a burst of remaining tokens. Suspect backpressure or chunking buffer edge-case in node/nginx/proxy layer.

What I saw: (recap from reproducer)
- Repro is easier when: sequence_length ~ 1024, batching enabled, KV cache reuse, and when client slowly reads (simulated 50ms read interval).
- More frequent under Dedicated GPU with quantized models vs hosted.

Hypotheses:
1) Runtime is buffering output until a full chunk boundary (X bytes or X tokens) and client read pacing interacts poorly with continuous batching-> stalls.
2) Proxy (nginx or envoy) chunked transfer encoding handling + keepalive heuristics triggering flush suppression.
3) Node SSE packer uses setTimeout debounce for coalescing chunks; high load increases debounce window.
4) Backpressure signals from downstream (net socket 'drain' backpressure) not being propagated up to serving runtime fast enough, causing write() to return false and then later drain coalesces bursts.

Repro steps (local minimal):
1) Start minimal server (local reproducer):
   - checkout branch: reproducer/streaming-kv-bp
   - node server: node examples/streaming-repro/server.js --port 8081

2) Repro client (slow reader):
   - Python client (slow-read):
     python3 examples/streaming-repro/slow_reader.py --url http://localhost:8081/generate --read-interval-ms 50 --seq-len 1024

3) Curl for quick peek (doesn't reliably show timing issues because it reads fast):
   curl -N -v http://localhost:8081/generate

Observed logs (server side):
- server logs (timestamps truncated):
  [2025-02-17T11:24:05Z] req=abcd1234 start stream
  [2025-02-17T11:24:05Z] req=abcd1234 batch=12 seq=1024 kv_hit=true
  [2025-02-17T11:24:05Z] req=abcd1234 sending chunk size=512
  [2025-02-17T11:24:05Z] req=abcd1234 write() returned true
  [2025-02-17T11:24:05Z] req=abcd1234 flush scheduled debounce=20ms
  [2025-02-17T11:24:07Z] req=abcd1234 client read paused (client_read_timeout)
  [2025-02-17T11:24:09Z] req=abcd1234 write() returned false (socket full)
  [2025-02-17T11:24:16Z] req=abcd1234 socket drain -> sending remainder (burst)

- Proxy logs (envoy/nginx):
  envoy: upstream_write_time high for req=abcd1234  (delay 7s)
  nginx: proxy_buffering on; flushed 1 chunk(s) late

Client-side capture (python slow-reader):
- Received: <initial meta chunk>
- Wait ~7s with no bytes
- Suddenly got remaining tokens in one large burst

Commands I ran (to inspect socket/backpressure):
- tcpdump capture: sudo tcpdump -i lo -w /tmp/sse-repro.pcap port 8081
- ss to see socket states: ss -tanp | grep 8081
- strace on node process (watch write/syscall timings): sudo strace -tt -p <pid> -e trace=write,sendto,sendmsg
- lsof -p <pid> | grep TCP

What changed when I tweaked parameters:
- If client read-interval <= 5ms, issue disappears (client keeps draining).
- Disabling batching in runtime (batch_size=1) reduces incidence to near-zero.
- Setting server SSE chunk debounce to 0ms removes stalls but increases small packet count (more CPU).
- On Dedicated infra (NVMe-backed IPC), stalls slightly worse than locally (more coalescing happening).

Quick local patches tried: (results)
- Force socket.setNoDelay(true) on server: no change (still see stalls).
- Explicit res.flushHeaders() after first chunk: reduces first stall but later chunks still coalesce.
- Change chunker to flush on token boundary rather than debounce: seems promising (fewer stalls in tests).
- Add explicit process.nextTick(() => socket.write(...)) instead of immediate write: made it worse (more coalescing).

Next investigative steps (todo):
- Add high-res timing to write() syscall (wrap net.Socket.write) to see when OS-level send buffers fill.
- Reproduce with envoy vs nginx vs direct client to isolate proxy behavior.
- Capture pcap and inspect TCP segments to determine whether the delay is at application or TCP layer (i.e., are segments queued in kernel or being delayed by app).
- Instrument down to uv_write/uv_buf_t if we suspect libuv coalescing on Node.
- Add a test that simulates slow-reader in CI to detect regressions.

Notes / links: 
- Related issue: INF-3421 (Jira) — initial report from support customer.
- PR that touched SSE chunk debounce: PR #876 (serving-runtime).

Scratch console commands used during debugging:
- tail -F /var/log/serving-runtime/serving.log | grep "req=abcd1234"
- jq to pretty print JSON bodies: echo '"$RAW"' | jq .
- run repro harness: ./bin/repro --clients 50 --read-delay-ms 50 --seq-len 1024

Potential mitigation options (short term):
- Expose SSE chunk debounce config (ms) as runtime knob per-route; default 0ms for dedicated workloads.
- Add heuristics: if socket.write returns false, immediately pause batching for that client until drain event.
- If downstream proxy present, recommend proxy config: proxy_buffering off (nginx) or appropriate flush settings in envoy.

Questions for SRE / infra:
- Are there TCP-level rate-limiting/packet coalescing settings on Dedicated clusters (tcp_sndbuf / tcp_cork)?
- Any sidecar or mesh layer that may coalesce writes for efficiency?

Short-term checklist to land patch: 
- [ ] Perf testcase added (slow-reader)
- [ ] Add socket.write() timing logs behind flag
- [ ] Add flush-on-token boundary variant and toggle
- [ ] Discuss proxy default config for streaming endpoints with infra

Appendix: Example minimal server reproducer (node)

// examples/streaming-repro/server.js (trimmed)
const http = require('http');
const { generateStream } = require('./fake-model');
http.createServer((req,res)=>{
  res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache' });
  const stream = generateStream({seqLen:1024});
  stream.on('data', chunk => {
    // chunk debounce (this is the suspect)
    setTimeout(()=>{
      const ok = res.write(`data: ${chunk}

`);
      if(!ok){
        // track backpressure
        console.log('write returned false');
      }
    }, 20); // try 0ms to compare
  });
  stream.on('end', ()=> res.end());
}).listen(8081);

Example slow-reader (python):
# examples/streaming-repro/slow_reader.py
import requests
import time
resp = requests.get('http://localhost:8081/generate', stream=True)
for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=64):
    if chunk:
        print('recv', len(chunk))
        time.sleep(0.05)
